name: MongoDB Atlas
scope_notes: Atlas cloud service; Admin API credentials (service accounts, legacy API keys) manage Atlas but cannot read cluster data, while database users read data; database auditing, access history and workload federation need dedicated (M10+) clusters.

controls.name: Require IP Access List for the Atlas Administration API
controls.what: Rejects Admin API requests from service accounts or API keys without a matching access list entry.
controls.setting: Organization Settings > Require IP Access List for the Atlas Administration API; API field apiAccessListRequired

controls.name: API Access List (per service account / API key)
controls.what: Limits each credential to listed IPs or CIDRs.
controls.setting: Applications > Service Accounts/API Keys > Edit > Add Access List Entry; /orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts/{clientId}/accessList, /orgs/{orgId}/apiKeys/{apiUserId}/accessList

controls.name: maxServiceAccountSecretValidityInHours
controls.what: Caps how long new service account secrets can be valid (8 to 8760 hours).

controls.name: Client Secret Expiration
controls.what: Each secret expires after a chosen duration of 8 hours to 365 days.
controls.setting: Create Service Account > Client Secret Expiration

controls.name: Atlas roles
controls.what: Org and project roles limit which Admin API operations the credential can perform.

controls.name: Delete service account / delete secret
controls.what: Removes the account (from all projects) or one secret.
controls.setting: Applications > Service Accounts > Delete; DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts/{clientId}, DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts/{clientId}/secrets/{secretId}

controls.name: Delete API key
controls.what: Deletes the key and removes it from all projects.
controls.setting: Applications > API Keys > Delete; atlas organizations apiKeys delete

controls.name: Temporary User
controls.what: Database user is deleted automatically after 6 hours, 1 day or 1 week.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > Add New Database User > Temporary User

controls.name: Restrict access to specific clusters
controls.what: Limits a database user to chosen clusters and federated database instances.
controls.setting: Database user > Restrict Access to Specific Clusters

controls.name: Project IP access list
controls.what: Only listed IPs can connect to clusters.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > IP Access List

controls.name: Delete database user
controls.what: Removes the database user; also the only way to revoke an X.509 user.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > Database Users > Delete

controls.name: Organization Owner role required to create service accounts and API keys
controls.what: Only Organization Owners can create org-level service accounts and API keys; project-level ones are created by project roles and are added to the org as Organization Member.

controls.name: Roles required to add database users
controls.what: Only users with the listed Organization or Project roles can create database users of any authentication type.

controls.name: Disconnect identity provider (Workload Identity Federation)
controls.what: Disconnecting the workload IdP from the organization removes Workload Identity Federation access for its users.
controls.setting: Federation management > Workload Identity Federation card > Manage > Disconnect

controls.name: Revoke JWKS
controls.what: Immediately drops JSON Web Key Sets cached on MongoDB nodes so tokens signed with a compromised key fail.
controls.setting: Federation management > Workload Identity Federation card > Manage > Revoke JWKS

no_control.what: Atlas-managed X.509 certificates cannot be revoked individually; only deleting the user removes access.

controls_unknown: Whether an org can block creation of legacy API keys entirely.
Whether API keys have any expiry setting.
Whether deleting a service account or secret invalidates already-issued 1-hour access tokens.
Whether deleting a database user terminates open connections.
Whether Admin API read (GET) calls are recorded anywhere; Activity Feed documents changes, not reads.
Default secret expiration value for service accounts.

credentials.name: Service account (Atlas Administration API, OAuth 2.0 client credentials)

authentication.summary: Client ID and secret (prefix mdb_sa_sk_) are exchanged at POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token for a 1-hour bearer token. Grants Admin API access only, not UI or cluster data.

federation.details: Separate credential, not tied to Atlas federated login. Docs say UI session timeout settings do not apply to service accounts; no statement on IdP conditional access.

ip_restriction.boundary: Per-service-account API access list; org can require a list for every Admin API request (403 otherwise). Applies to using tokens, not issuing or revoking them; does not cover Atlas CLI or App Connections delegated access.

lifetime.summary: Token 1 h; secret 8 h to 365 days, org-capped

renewal.expiry_basis: Access token expires after 1 hour and cannot be refreshed; secret expires on its set date.
renewal.summary: Request a new token with the client secret; rotate by adding a new secret (old one is cut to 7 days).

administration.summary: Org Owners create org service accounts; project-level accounts need Project Owner. Roles scope access.
administration.conditions: Org Owner needed to manage a project service account that also has org or other-project access.

offboard.details: Service accounts are their own principals that belong to an organization, not to a user.

inventory.details: Organization Owners can view all service accounts (Identity & Access > Applications) or call GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts.

reads.ui: Project > Security > Activity Feed > Filter > Event = database user added (MONGODB_USER_ADDED); add Initiated By filter for the key/service account

token_format.notes: Prefix on the client secret; access tokens are bearer tokens with expires_in 3600.

log_sources.name: Organization / Project Activity Feed
log_sources.notes: All tiers; UI, atlas events CLI, GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/events and /groups/{groupId}/events; org feed kept for life of the org; exportable to SIEM/OTel.

credential_id_fields.notes: Identifies the API key that triggered the event; whether service accounts populate it is not documented.

anomaly_cues: New secret added to an existing service account
Access list entry added for unfamiliar IP or 0.0.0.0/0
Service account added to new projects or roles raised
Database user created by a service account

containment.steps: Revoke tokens via POST /api/oauth/revoke, delete the secret or the service account, remove access list entries.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether deleting the secret invalidates issued tokens; revoke tokens explicitly. Tokens last at most 1 hour.

unknown: Whether token issuance or individual API calls are logged

calls.reveals: Creates a database user to read cluster data (Admin API cannot read data directly)

unknown: Whether GET calls appear in any log

authentication.summary: Public key plus private key used with HTTP Digest auth on each Admin API request. Legacy; MongoDB recommends service accounts.

federation.details: Cannot log into the UI; UI session timeouts do not apply. No doc statement on IdP conditional access.

ip_restriction.boundary: Per-key API access list; org setting can require a list for every request. Not applied to Atlas CLI user logins or App Connections.

renewal.summary: Same key pair reused on every request until deleted.

administration.summary: Org Owners create org keys; Project Owners create project keys. Private key shown once. Roles scope access.

offboard.details: API keys belong to an organization, not to a user.

inventory.details: Organization Owners can view all API keys or call GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/apiKeys.

usage.ui: Organization > Configurations > Activity Feed (or Project > Security > Activity Feed) > Filter > Initiated By

reads.ui: Project > Security > Activity Feed > Filter > Event = database user added (MONGODB_USER_ADDED); add Initiated By filter for the key/service account

token_format.notes: Public/private key pair; no documented prefix.

log_sources.name: Organization / Project Activity Feed
log_sources.notes: All tiers; API and SIEM export.

credential_id_fields.notes: Present when an API key triggered the event (userId omitted).

anomaly_cues: Old keys with no expiry still active

containment.steps: Delete the API key (UI, atlas organizations apiKeys delete, or Admin API).
containment.notes: Digest auth checks the key on each request, so deletion should stop further calls; not explicitly stated.

calls.reveals: System status and API key metadata
Creates a database user for data access
